info.name: Banking Transactions API
info.description:
Homework 1 - in-memory banking transactions service (Express 5).

- **Auth:** none.
- **Content type:** JSON requests and responses.
- **Base URL:** `{{baseUrl}}` (default `http://localhost:3000`, port from `PORT`).

Run folders in order: *Create transaction* saves `depositId`, used by later requests.
Every request has test scripts, so the collection can run with `postman collection run`.

item.name: Create transaction
item.description:
`POST /transactions` — records a transaction. Body must be a JSON object with `Content-Type: application/json` (max 100kb).

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | yes | `deposit` \| `withdrawal` \| `transfer` |
| `amount` | yes | JSON number, `> 0`, `<= 1000000000`, at most 2 decimal places |
| `currency` | yes | Uppercase ISO 4217, one of: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, CAD, AUD, CNY, SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN, CZK, UAH |
| `fromAccount` | withdrawal, transfer | `ACC-` + 5 letters/digits (case-sensitive); must be absent or `null` for deposit |
| `toAccount` | deposit, transfer | Same format; must be absent or `null` for withdrawal; must differ from `fromAccount` |
| `timestamp` | no | ISO 8601 with seconds and timezone (`Z` or `±hh:mm`), not in the future. Defaults to server time; stored as UTC |

Any other field is rejected (`id`, `status`, `failureReason` are server-set). All problems are reported at once.

**201 Created** + `Location: /transactions/{id}`
```json
{ "id": "uuid", "fromAccount": "ACC-12345 | null", "toAccount": "ACC-67890 | null", "amount": 100.5,
  "currency": "USD", "type": "deposit", "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z", "status": "completed" }
```
**Status rules:** a deposit is always `completed`. A withdrawal or transfer is `completed` only if `fromAccount` holds enough funds **in that currency** (completed transactions only, checked in arrival order, whatever `timestamp` says).
Otherwise it is still stored and returned with **201**, but with `status: "failed"` and an extra field `failureReason: "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS"`. `failureReason` appears only on failed transactions.

The deposits below fund the withdrawal and transfer that follow, so those complete.

item.name: Create transaction - validation errors
item.description:
Expected: **400** with
```json
{ "error": "Validation failed", "details": [{ "field": "...", "message": "..." }] }
```
`details` lists every problem in field order (`fromAccount`, `toAccount`, `amount`, `currency`, `type`, `timestamp`), then unknown fields.

item.name: Empty object - all required fields missing

request.description: An empty body with JSON content type behaves the same.

exec: pm.expect(body.details).to.eql([{"field": "amount", "message": "Amount is required"}, {"field": "currency", "message": "Currency is required"}, {"field": "type", "message": "Type is required"}]);

request.description: Arrays, or a request without `Content-Type: application/json`, are rejected as a whole.

exec: pm.expect(body.details).to.eql([{"field": "body", "message": "Request body must be a JSON object"}]);

request.description: Unparseable JSON, or a top-level primitive such as `"x"` or `null`.
The pre-request script builds a ~110kb body. Expected **413** with the same error shape.
`id`, `status`, `failureReason` are set by the server; any other extra field is unknown.

request.description: Zero and negative amounts are rejected.

item.name: Filter transactions
item.description:
`GET /transactions` with filters. All filters are optional and combine with **AND**; the result keeps the newest-first order.

| Param | Rule |
|---|---|
| `accountId` | `ACC-XXXXX`; matches `fromAccount` **or** `toAccount` |
| `type` | `deposit` \| `withdrawal` \| `transfer` |
| `status` | `pending` \| `completed` \| `failed` |
| `from`, `to` | `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC day; a date-only `to` includes the whole day, up to `23:59:59.999Z`) or an ISO 8601 date-time with a timezone. Both ends inclusive, `from <= to`, future dates allowed |

In a query string an unencoded `+` becomes a space, so write an offset as `%2B02:00` or use `Z`. Repeated, empty or unknown parameters give **400**, and every problem is reported at once.

Run after *Create transaction*: the tests check that each result matches its filter, not exact counts, so the collection can run repeatedly on the same server.

item.name: Account balance
item.description:
`GET /accounts/:accountId/balance` — balance per currency, from **completed** transactions only. Currencies are never added together.

- Deposits add to `toAccount`, withdrawals subtract from `fromAccount`, transfers do both.
- A currency is listed once the account has any completed transaction in it; a net zero shows as `0`.
- An account with no completed transactions returns `200` with `balance: {}` (not 404).
- A malformed `accountId` gives **400**. The endpoint takes **no query parameters**: any one gives **400** `Unknown query parameter "<name>"`, reported together with an `accountId` error.

**200**
```json
{ "accountId": "ACC-12345", "balance": { "USD": 1000000100.51, "EUR": 0 } }
```
Exact amounts depend on how many times the collection has run against the same server, so the tests check the shape, not the totals.

item.name: Account summary
item.description:
`GET /accounts/:accountId/summary` — an at-a-glance view of one account.

- `totalDeposits` / `totalWithdrawals`: per currency, **completed** transactions only. An incoming transfer counts as a deposit, an outgoing one as a withdrawal, so for each currency deposits − withdrawals = balance. Both totals list the same currencies as the balance, with `0` for a side without movement.
- `transactionCount`, `failedCount`, `mostRecentTransactionDate`: cover **all** of the account's transactions, failed ones included.
- No transactions: `{}`, `{}`, `0`, `0`, `null`.
- A malformed `accountId` gives **400**; the endpoint takes **no query parameters** (any one gives **400**).

**200**
```json
{ "accountId": "ACC-12345", "totalDeposits": { "USD": 1000, "EUR": 250 }, "totalWithdrawals": { "USD": 0, "EUR": 250 },
  "transactionCount": 7, "failedCount": 0, "mostRecentTransactionDate": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z" }
```
Totals grow with every run against the same server, so the tests check the contract, not exact numbers.
